spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:201-219 - after each attempt, judge.detector.judge_meltdown(...) is called (lines 195-199) and 'if meltdown_judgment.is_meltdown:' returns RunResult with stop_reason=StopReason.MELTDOWN_TRIGGERED, breaking the loop. is_meltdown becomes True at judge.py:351 ('severity.value >= MODERATE and len(signals) >= 2'), which fires for CRITICAL severity (judge.py:339-340) but also for any MODERATE+. So a CRITICAL meltdown does end the test (and the stop fires even earlier than CRITICAL).
spec_features.notes: The stop is actually broader than the claim: it triggers at MODERATE+, not only CRITICAL. CRITICAL is one of the conditions that stops the loop, and the stop is genuinely enforced (early return). The stop ends the test the moment meltdown is measured rather than protecting/debriefing the subject.
